docs.title: Platforms
docs.text: Pantheon runs only on OpenCode. Multi-platform adapters were removed in v1.0; Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, Cline, Continue.dev, and VS Code Copilot are not supported. This page is an overview and links out. It does not restate the support matrix — that is Compatibility.

docs.title: Form factors
docs.text: OpenCode ships as a terminal TUI, a desktop app, and an IDE extension. Pantheon's agents, skills, and instructions are discovered from the project directory the same way in each. The desktop app adds integrated diffs, file-tree browsing, and native notifications; it is not a separate installation model.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
Use the installer, not manual copying:

npx pantheon-opencode init            # global
npx pantheon-opencode init --project  # project-local

The installer registers Pantheon's runtime integrations automatically. It writes the singular plugin key for OpenCode V1 and the plural plugins key for OpenCode V2; do not add either key by hand. Flags, backup, uninstall, and reconcile are in Installation.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
OpenCode reads opencode.json (or opencode.jsonc) from the project root. The installer writes opencode.json; a V2 host may also merge a sibling .jsonc — see Compatibility.

default_agent: zeus and permission.skill are seeded by the installer, not shipped as a template file. The published package carries no opencode.json template. Contributors who keep a project-level config for their own sessions should leave it untracked.

Agent definitions live in src/agents/*.md; the installer copies them into the selected config tree. Editing an installed copy does not persist — the next init overwrites it. Edit the canonical source instead.

docs.title: File locations
docs.text:
Project install:

your-project/
├── opencode.json
├── AGENTS.md
├── .opencode/agents/
├── .opencode/skills/
├── .opencode/instructions/
├── .opencode/prompts/
└── .pantheon/

Global install:

~/.config/opencode/
├── opencode.json
├── AGENTS.md
├── agents/
├── skills/
├── instructions/
├── scripts/          # installed MCP entrypoints
└── tui.json          # V1 TUI registration

The V2 TUI uses a local plugin directory instead of tui.json. See OpenCode V2.

docs.title: Quick reference
docs.text:
Action Command Start OpenCode (TUI) opencode Run non-interactively opencode run "prompt" Initialize project rules /init in-session Invoke an agent @zeus: implement email verification List agents opencode agent list List models opencode models Add an MCP server opencode mcp add Add a provider key opencode auth login List sessions opencode session list Token stats opencode stats

/init is OpenCode's built-in project-context generator. It is complementary to Pantheon: /init captures project-level conventions, while Pantheon agents supply role behavior. If AGENTS.md already exists, /init improves it in place.

docs.title: ACP (Agent Client Protocol)
docs.text:
OpenCode can run as an ACP-compatible agent for editors such as Zed, JetBrains, or Neovim. Start the server with opencode acp; it communicates over JSON-RPC on stdio. ACP does not change the selected plugin contract: V1 hook/delegate behavior still depends on V1 host events, and the V2 plugin remains its own surface. Verify the registration in opencode.json before relying on a feature.

For Zed, add this to ~/.config/zed/settings.json:

{
  "agent_servers": {
    "OpenCode": {
      "type": "custom",
      "command": "opencode",
      "args": ["acp"]
    }
  }
}

type: "custom" is the field Zed's settings schema uses for a hand-configured agent server rather than a built-in one.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Symptom Check Agents not showing up opencode agent list; valid YAML frontmatter; correct agents directory Default agent not working default_agent must match an agent with mode: primary Model not available provider/model format; opencode models; provider key Instructions not loading Paths are relative to the config file; global and project layers merge MCP server not connecting opencode mcp list; OAuth via opencode mcp auth <server> Skills not discovered permission.skill allows the skill; skills are installed Slow responses Cheaper model for discovery; fewer instruction files

For MCP-specific failures, see MCP. For installer and driver problems, see Installation.

docs.title: Dynamic prompts
docs.text: OpenCode prompt files support {file:path} interpolation. Pantheon's /pantheon council prompt uses that to build a dynamic, per-run prompt. The generation script and its limits are described in the prompt file itself (prompts/); static prompt templates remain the default for the other commands.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text: The first ten minutes: install, restart, dispatch, and read the first result. Installer flags, exit codes, saved plans, backups, and uninstall have their own home in Installation.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text: You need OpenCode and a supported Node.js. The exact versions and the per-host evidence are in Compatibility. Python is only needed for the optional MCP servers.

docs.title: 1. Install
docs.text:
From the project where you want to use Pantheon:

npx pantheon-opencode init

The interactive setup chooses components and a global or project location before reviewing the apply. Canceling writes nothing.

docs.title: 2. Restart OpenCode
docs.text:
opencode

Restart is required after installing or changing the plugin generation. A restart reloads the selected plugin; it is not an automatic resume of delegated work.

docs.title: 3. Check the install
docs.text:
npx pantheon-opencode doctor

doctor validates the installed package, the plugin registration, the MCP servers, and drift between the installed version and the running package. A healthy install reports no warning.

docs.title: 4. Dispatch your first task
docs.text:
Describe the outcome, not the steps:

/pantheon Add CSV export to the reports page, including tests and a review.

Or open the dispatch panel to watch delegated work:

/dispatch

/dispatch opens the same delegation tree the sidebar summarizes, with one row per child and detail for the selected child. It needs an open session.

docs.title: What you should see
docs.text:
• Zeus routes the request. Bounded work goes to one specialist; planning, discovery, and review are added when scope and risk call for them.
  • When a plan is requested, Athena returns it to Zeus, who displays the full plan in the main conversation before asking for approval.
  • Implementation agents return ## subtask_summary; investigations return structured findings. A child that returns nothing is surfaced as an error, not as a silent success.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Installation — flags, saved plans, backup, uninstall, reconcile, MCP pins.
  • OpenCode V2 — sidebar block, /dispatch panel, context pruning, memory injection, session goals.
  • MCP and MCP Tools — servers and tool signatures.
  • Memory — what is stored, for how long, and when to search.

docs.title: Pantheon Release Process
docs.text: How versioning, releases, and packaging work.

docs.title: Versioning Policy
docs.text:
Pantheon follows Semantic Versioning based on Conventional Commits:

Commit pattern Version bump BREAKING CHANGE or type!: in scope MAJOR (x.0.0) feat: MINOR (x.y.0) fix:, chore:, docs:, refactor:, etc. PATCH (x.y.z)

Candidate version: the manifests in this checkout express the version being prepared; they do not confirm a publication. A beta is published only after the Release workflow completes successfully. To check which version is actually published, consult the npm beta dist-tag.

docs.title: Version Commands
docs.text:
# Show current version, latest stable git tag, and pending release status
node scripts/versioning.mjs status

# Sync all manifests + promote [Unreleased] → [vX.Y.Z] (recommended bump)
node scripts/versioning.mjs apply          # type auto (from commits)
node scripts/versioning.mjs apply minor    # explicit type: patch | minor | major
node scripts/versioning.mjs apply --notes  # pre-fill the promoted entry with
                                           # release notes generated from commits

# Advance the committed beta line (X.Y.Z-beta.N → X.Y.Z-beta.(N+1)) and
# promote [Unreleased] → [vX.Y.Z-beta.N], exactly like the stable path.
node scripts/versioning.mjs apply --beta
node scripts/versioning.mjs beta           # alias for apply --beta

# Merge pending notes into an already-promoted candidate without a version bump
node scripts/versioning.mjs changelog 1.6.0-beta.10

# Generate release notes from conventional commits (lastTag..HEAD)
node scripts/release-notes.mjs             # stable vX.Y.Z tags only
node scripts/release-notes.mjs --draft     # last 30 commits, no tag lookup

# CI-side consistency check (run in the `validate` job of ci.yml)
node scripts/version-check.mjs

# Dry-run of the release payload (status + release notes + pack)
npm run release:dry-run

docs.title: beta.5: rebuild the TUI bundle AFTER the version bump — dist embeds the
package version and the CI "TUI dist freshness" gate fails otherwise.
docs.text:
npm install --prefix src/plugins/tui && npm run build --prefix src/plugins/tui

apply syncs the version manifests (package.json, plugin.json, pyproject.toml, src/plugins/tui/package.json) and promotes the [Unreleased] changelog section to a versioned entry. apply --beta (alias beta) does the same: it syncs the manifests to the next committed X.Y.Z-beta.N and promotes [Unreleased] to ## [vX.Y.Z-beta.N]. Do not edit CHANGELOG.md by hand. When the target version section already exists, versioning.mjs changelog <version> merges [Unreleased] into that section and resets the template without advancing the package version or duplicating the release heading. Release validation also keeps the root pair (package.json + package-lock.json) and the TUI pair (src/plugins/tui/package.json + src/plugins/tui/package-lock.json) in the same versioned inventory. The TUI is a root workspace, so CI installs both with a single npm ci --ignore-scripts at the root; the nested TUI lock is still versioned and still shipped because the user-facing postinstall syncs against it. It no longer creates git tags — tags are workflow-owned (see below).

docs.title: Version Bump (the only manual step)
docs.text:
1. Create a branch off main.
  2. Bump the version: 
    node scripts/versioning.mjs apply minor   # or patch/major
    or edit package.json directly — the version is the release signal. The TUI manifest (src/plugins/tui/package.json) carries the same version; npm run version:check fails when the two drift. node_modules/ state is irrelevant here: the TUI is a root workspace, so one root npm ci --ignore-scripts installs it.
  3. Fill in the promoted changelog section with the release notes for the upcoming version. The release body is extracted from this section, so it must exist and be accurate.
  4. Commit + push + open a PR to main. Review the complete working-tree diff, then stage every intentional release change: all outputs produced by versioning.mjs and any release docs deliberately edited. The paths below are illustrative and incomplete; check the full diff rather than treating this list as exhaustive. In particular, do not omit src/plugins/tui/dist/tui.js: the bundle embeds the package version and CI checks TUI dist freshness. Leave unrelated changes and untracked RED tests out of the release commit.
git status --short
git diff
git add CHANGELOG.md docs/RELEASING.md package.json package-lock.json \
  plugin.json pyproject.toml src/plugins/tui/package.json \
  src/plugins/tui/package-lock.json src/plugins/tui/dist/tui.js
# Add any other intentional paths found while reviewing the complete diff.
git diff --cached --check
git diff --cached --name-only
git diff --cached
git commit -m "chore(release): vX.Y.Z"
git push -u origin <branch>
  1. Wait for CI. The PR must pass validate (version manifests, engine, packaging, sandbox), test-suite, plugin-v2-ts-coverage, commitlint, security-scan, and CodeQL before merging. ci.yml also runs on pushes to main, so the merged SHA carries its own CI evidence.

No tag is created locally. Merging an ordinary PR does not release. To publish a stable version, use the explicit Release workflow dispatch after the intended commit is on main; it validates manifests and preserves the exact target-SHA/idempotency checks.

docs.title: Release Notes
docs.text: Release notes are generated from conventional commits, never written from scratch. Commitlint (12 types / 40 scopes) validates every commit before it merges, so the generator can always group the history.

docs.title: Type → section mapping
docs.text:
Release notes use the final emoji group format — 🆕 What's New / 🐞 Fixed / ⚠️ Known Issues / ✅ Closed Issues:

Commit type Release notes section feat, perf, docs ## 🆕 What's New (docs are user-facing — no dedicated group) fix, security ## 🐞 Fixed --known-issues "text" (CLI flag, repeatable) ## ⚠️ Known Issues (omitted when the flag is absent — never emitted empty) Closes #N / Fixes #N / Resolves #N in the commit body ## ✅ Closed Issues — bullet - #N - <subject> (deduped; omitted when no refs exist) chore, refactor, test, ci, build, style, revert (and unknown types) omitted — internal, never user-facing BREAKING CHANGE footer or type!: / type(scope)!: 💥 prefix on the bullet inside What's New (e.g. - 💥 **scope** — subject) — no dedicated Breaking group

Merge commits ("Merge …") and empty-subject chores are skipped. Bullets use - **<scope>** — <subject> (the scope as the bold prefix; without a scope the whole subject is bolded). Section order is What's New → Fixed → Known Issues → Closed Issues.

docs.title: Generate the notes
docs.text:
# Commits since the latest stable tag (strict vX.Y.Z, pre-releases excluded)
node scripts/release-notes.mjs

# Same output without reading git tags (last 30 commits) — quick preview or
# pre-first-tag use
node scripts/release-notes.mjs --draft

# Add a manual Known Issues entry (repeatable; omitted from output when absent)
node scripts/release-notes.mjs --known-issues "widget API is unstable"

# Pre-merge review: version status + generated notes + pack dry-run
npm run release:dry-run

The script exits 0 whenever it can generate. stdout is markdown ready to paste into the [Unreleased] CHANGELOG section (diagnostics go to stderr).

docs.title: Release body by channel
docs.text:
release.yml extracts the release body from the committed CHANGELOG.md for both dispatch channels; only the stable channel attaches it to a GitHub Release:

Channel Notes source stable node scripts/changelog-extract.mjs X.Y.Z reads the curated ## [X.Y.Z] section from CHANGELOG.md; the dispatch fails if the section is missing. Used as the GitHub Release body. beta node scripts/changelog-extract.mjs X.Y.Z-beta.N reads the curated ## [X.Y.Z-beta.N] section from CHANGELOG.md; the dispatch fails if the section is missing. Carried in the release artifact only — beta creates no GitHub Release. recovery Static note (Recovery publish for existing tag ...); the original notes are not regenerated.

The version is committed, so a CHANGELOG.md section is authorable before the dispatch and is required for both channels. Beta does not use generated conventional-commit notes.

docs.title: Flow
docs.text:
1. Commit — Conventional Commits enforced by commitlint (local hook + CI).
  2. Generate — node scripts/release-notes.mjs → paste the output into the [Unreleased] section, or let apply --notes do it automatically.
  3. CHANGELOG — node scripts/versioning.mjs apply minor [--notes] bumps the manifests and promotes [Unreleased] → [vX.Y.Z]. With --notes the promoted entry is pre-filled from the grouped commits (mapped to the final emoji groups ## 🆕 What's New / 🐞 Fixed / ⚠️ Known Issues / ✅ Closed Issues); without it the flow stays manual. --notes replaces any manual [Unreleased] content — review the diff before committing.
  4. Release body by channel — node scripts/changelog-extract.mjs <version> pulls the curated versioned section into the GitHub Release body for both stable (X.Y.Z) and beta (X.Y.Z-beta.N), and fails if the section is missing; recovery uses a static note and does not regenerate notes.
  5. Publish — the workflow tags the exact dispatch target SHA and publishes to npm (stable or beta per the release_channel input).

docs.title: Stable Release (manual dispatch)
docs.text:
Dispatching .github/workflows/release.yml without recovery inputs runs the stable release path:

  1. Type: channel=stable, npm dist-tag=latest.
  2. Version gate — package.json must be a clean X.Y.Z and not strictly behind the latest stable git tag (exact vX.Y.Z tags only; -beta.* pre-release tags are excluded from the comparison). Fails loudly if the version was never bumped.
  3. Pack and verify — the validation job packs exactly one immutable npm tarball with lifecycle scripts disabled. It records that tarball's SHA-256 together with the full TARGET_SHA; the release job recomputes the digest and rejects any mismatch.
  4. Idempotent guard — if tag vX.Y.Z exists AND its GitHub Release exists, exit 0 (already released). If the tag exists but the release is missing, continue and complete the release (tag creation is skipped).
  5. Release body — node scripts/changelog-extract.mjs X.Y.Z extracts the ## [X.Y.Z] - date section from CHANGELOG.md into the runner temp path $RUNNER_TEMP/release-notes.md (published as release-artifact/release-notes.md); fails if the section is missing.
  6. Tag creation (workflow-owned) — a tag ref is created through the repository-scoped GitHub API on the exact dispatch target SHA.
  7. GitHub Release — gh release create vX.Y.Z --target <dispatch-sha> --verify-tag --title "Pantheon vX.Y.Z" --notes-file release-artifact/release-notes.md.
  8. npm publish (final step) — gated by the idempotency lookup, then that same tarball (without repacking) is published with --tag latest --access public --provenance. The SHA-256 validated in the validation job is therefore the SHA-256 of the file published to npm.

A global concurrency group (release, no cancel-in-progress) serializes runs so beta and stable paths can never double-publish.

docs.title: Package and evidence contract
docs.text:
The release evidence is fail-closed and has one artifact identity:

  • root dependencies and the TUI workspace use one npm ci --ignore-scripts with package.json and package-lock.json;
  • the TUI manifest and lockfile remain independently validated as package and publish evidence;
  • a release creates one npm .tgz tarball, computes one SHA-256, and carries that exact file and digest from validation to publication; a second npm pack is not a valid replacement;
  • the tarball and GitHub tag/release are bound to the same full TARGET_SHA.

Any npm ci failure blocks the run. There is no npm install fallback, and PANTHEON_ALLOW_NPM_INSTALL_FALLBACK is not part of the current contract.

docs.title: Six release gates
docs.text:
The validate job of release.yml runs six gates on the frozen TARGET_SHA. Each prints GATE <name>: PASS and writes a named evidence file to $RUNNER_TEMP/gate-evidence/<name>.json; the directory is uploaded as release-gate-evidence-<run_id> (90-day retention). There is no fallback: a command that cannot run, a missing artifact, an unsupported host, or a SKIP is a failed gate, and a failed gate aborts before the artifact upload and before any release credential is exposed.

Gate Executed by Fails when Evidence (a) tests scripts/release-gates.mjs tests: pytest + src/mcp coverage ≥ 80, test:node, test:ts, coverage:plugin-v2, test:install; pytest runs in an isolated venv built from src/mcp/requirements-mcp.txt any suite, coverage threshold, or the mandatory install tier fails; an unsatisfiable or unverified pin set fails the gate tests.json (b) host compatibility scripts/release-gates.mjs host: each measured host installed and exercised in an isolated sandbox; the gate reports a supported family with no row as "supported, unmeasured" instead of failing it a measured row fails, or a known-broken host is listed host.json (c) install scripts/release-gates.mjs install: the immutable .tgz installed globally, headless init, validate-sandbox-install.mjs, and a host-backed tool canary install, init, source comparison, MCP/doctor checks, or canary fails or skips install.json, install-canary.log (d) package scripts/release-gates.mjs package: SHA-256 recomputed over the same .tgz, payload inspected, package:validate the digest, name, version, target SHA, or payload disagree; no second npm pack is accepted package.json (e) changelog scripts/release-gates.mjs changelog: changelog-extract.mjs the [version] section is missing or empty; recovery checks the tag instead changelog.json, changelog.md (f) metadata scripts/release-gates.mjs metadata: version-check.mjs + validate-node-engine-policy.mjs manifests drift, the channel/version shape is wrong, or the SHA is not 40 hex metadata.json

The host evidence matrix is declared in release.yml (PANTHEON_RELEASE_MATRIX) and is validated by the gate, not trusted. Support is family-level: the gate requires no row per family, reports a family with no row as "supported, unmeasured", and fails only when a measured row fails or a known-broken host is listed. See Compatibility for the support policy and the known-broken set. A measured row that cannot run is a failure — the release path has no SKIP.

docs.title: Python test environment (gate a)
docs.text:
The Python suite imports fastmcp/mcp at collection time, so its verdict only means something against the pins in src/mcp/requirements-mcp.txt. Gate (a) therefore does not use the runner's ambient interpreter:

  • the validate job creates $RUNNER_TEMP/gate-venv with python3 -m venv from the interpreter pinned by actions/setup-python (python-version: '3.12', i.e. CPython 3.12.x on ubuntu-latest; the package metadata declares requires-python >= 3.11), installs coverage pytest pyyaml, pytest-asyncio==1.3.0, and -r src/mcp/requirements-mcp.txt -r src/mcp/requirements-vision.txt;
  • PANTHEON_PYTHON is exported to that venv and release-gates.mjs resolves every Python command through it. A set-but-missing or non-executable PANTHEON_PYTHON is a hard failure, never a fallback to the ambient python3;
  • pip check and an explicit assertion that every == pin in both requirements files is installed at exactly that version run before pytest. A failed venv creation, download, install, or pin assertion aborts the job (fail-closed via set -euo pipefail); no failure is downgraded to a skip;
  • actions/setup-python's cache: pip still applies: the venv's pip shares ~/.cache/pip, so the download cache is reused while the install itself stays isolated;
  • the CI test-suite job builds the same venv ($RUNNER_TEMP/ci-venv) and points PANTHEON_PYTHON at it, so CI and the release gate share one environment contract;
  • tests.json records the interpreter path and python --version used for the run.

Local equivalent of the gate's Python step:

python3 -m venv /tmp/pantheon-gate-venv
/tmp/pantheon-gate-venv/bin/python -m pip install -r src/mcp/requirements-mcp.txt -r src/mcp/requirements-vision.txt
PANTHEON_PYTHON=/tmp/pantheon-gate-venv/bin/python \
  node scripts/release-gates.mjs tests --evidence-dir /tmp/gate-evidence

Running pytest on an interpreter without these pins is not evidence: with fastmcp 3.4.2 / mcp 1.28.0 on PATH, tests/test_persistence_goals.py fails at collection by design, which is an environment defect, not a product defect.

docs.title: Test tiers
docs.text:
• Default (developer loop): npm run test:node runs tests/*.mjs and tests/pantheon/*.mjs excluding tests/install-opencode.test.mjs and tests/install-e2e.test.mjs. A bare node --test over those files skips their cases with an explicit reason unless the tier is opted into.
  • Heavy tier (optional locally, mandatory in release): npm run test:install sets PANTHEON_RUN_INSTALL_TESTS=1 and runs both real-install files. npm test / test:all does not include it, so the local loop stays fast; gate (a) always includes it.

docs.title: Coverage contract
docs.text:
• Required: Python src/mcp branch coverage ≥ 80% (coverage report --fail-under=80) and the src/plugin-v2.ts line measurement (npm run coverage:plugin-v2). Both run in gate (a).
  • Not PASS: Node coverage (npm run coverage) is report-only and enforces no threshold; TypeScript under src/ outside the plugin-v2 measurement is unmeasured. Neither may be cited as evidence that a threshold passed.
  • No new threshold is introduced by this contract.

docs.title: Memory MCP packaging
docs.text: src/mcp/memory_mcp.py is the canonical Memory MCP server. The scripts/memory_mcp.py source-tree entrypoint delegates to it, and the runtime installer copies the canonical source into the installed scripts directory. tests/test_mcp_scripts_sync.py checks that the compatibility entrypoint exposes the same tool list as the canonical server.

docs.title: Beta Releases (explicit dispatch with release_channel=beta)
docs.text:
Publication is authorized only by an explicit workflow_dispatch of release.yml. PR labels, pushes, merges, and tags never trigger or authorize a release. Dispatching with release_channel=beta runs the beta path; a beta recovery is triggered by a dispatch carrying recovery_version plus recovery_target_sha (and recovery_pr_number only for the legacy format); a dispatch without recovery inputs and release_channel=stable (the default) is the stable path.

  1. Type: channel=beta, npm dist-tag=beta.
  2. Committed version — apply --beta advanced package.json (and the other manifests) to X.Y.Z-beta.N before the dispatch. The workflow reads the committed version; it never computes a beta version and never queries npm for a baseline. A version that is not X.Y.Z-beta.N fails the gate.
  3. CHANGELOG — the bump PR must contain a ## [X.Y.Z-beta.N] - date section; the release body is extracted from it and the dispatch fails if it is missing. Beta does not use generated conventional-commit notes.
  4. Tag — the immutable tag vX.Y.Z-beta.N is created on the dispatch target SHA. Beta creates no GitHub Release: the official Zenodo ↔ GitHub integration archives every Release (pre-releases included), so a beta Release would add an unwanted version to the Zenodo family. The git tag alone backs by-tag recovery.
  5. npm publish --tag beta publishes the immutable artifact. The workflow does not create a PR comment.

docs.title: Beta npm-publish recovery (explicit dispatch)
docs.text:
If a beta's git tag already exists but npm publishing failed, rerun Release with recovery_version (the committed X.Y.Z-beta.N, without v) and recovery_target_sha (the full 40-hex commit SHA). The legacy X.Y.Z-beta.<pr>.<sha7> format is still accepted but additionally requires recovery_pr_number matching the version and the seven-character SHA suffix. For the current X.Y.Z-beta.N format only the version and SHA are needed. The workflow checks these values before checkout, requires the remote v<version> tag to exist on the recovery target SHA, and never creates or moves a tag or release in this mode (beta creates no GitHub Release, so recovery is bound to the tag alone). It packs the immutable checkout and publishes only when that exact npm version is absent; an existing npm version is a successful no-op. Partial or invalid inputs, a missing tag, API errors, and tag mismatches fail closed.

The recovery path is beta-only and does not calculate a new version or change the normal stable dispatch and beta-channel dispatch paths.

The pipeline is designed so reruns are safe:

  • Already fully released → the idempotent guard exits 0; nothing is re-tagged, re-released, or re-published.
  • Crash between tag push and release create (stable) → tag exists but release is missing; a rerun skips tag creation and completes the release. Beta creates no Release, so its reruns proceed to the npm step.
  • Crash after npm publish → a rerun hits the idempotent guard (exit 0), and the npm existence check prevents publishing the same version again.
  • changelog-extract fails on a stable or beta dispatch → the [X.Y.Z] / [X.Y.Z-beta.N] section is missing from CHANGELOG.md; add it in the bump PR and rerun. Both non-recovery channels extract the release body from the committed CHANGELOG.md; recovery uses a static note.

Before a manual rerun, verify the expected pre-run state (git tag, GitHub releases, and the npm version) directly against the live registries.

docs.title: npm Policy
docs.text:
Deprecate, never unpublish. A published package version is permanent — removing it breaks downstream installs and the npm_check idempotency gate. To retire a broken version:

npm deprecate pantheon-opencode@<ver> "reason: <why it should not be used>"

docs.title: Rollback
docs.text:
Manual step with human approval. The release workflow never rolls back — it publishes forward only. Re-pointing the npm latest tag is decided and executed by a maintainer, outside the automated path.

A rollback re-points the latest dist-tag. It does not delete the released artifact and it does not rewrite history.

docs.title: Trigger
docs.text: Roll back when a blocking defect is discovered after the stable publication and latest carries a regression that prevents use — for example an installer that cannot complete, or a package that does not start on the supported OpenCode line. A defect that can wait for the next patch does not qualify: publish forward instead.

docs.title: Restore the stable channel
docs.text:
npm dist-tag add pantheon-opencode@1.5.2 latest

Syntax: npm dist-tag add <package-spec (with version)> [<tag>] (npm dist-tag --help).

1.6.0 remains published on npm — only the latest pointer moves back to 1.5.2. Consumers without a lockfile resolve 1.5.2 again, while the regressed version stays reachable by exact version. Nothing is re-tagged on git, and no workflow runs.

docs.title: Do not
docs.text:
• Do not npm unpublish. Unpublishing is destructive and irreversible: it breaks every consumer whose lockfile pins the affected version, and it defeats the npm_check idempotency gate. Versions are deprecated, never removed (see npm Policy).
  • Do not rewrite the GitHub Release without a note. The Release is the published record of what shipped; editing or deleting it silently hides the incident from everyone who reads the changelog later.

docs.title: What a rollback does not undo
docs.text:
• Zenodo archival — once the GitHub Release exists, the Zenodo integration has deposited the record and version DOI. That deposit is irreversible.
  • The git tag — v1.6.0 stays on its commit. The tag is immutable and is not moved or deleted during a rollback.

docs.title: Required record
docs.text:
Log the rollback on the release (or the tracking issue) before or immediately after the command runs:

  • the defect that triggered it, with evidence;
  • the command executed, verbatim;
  • the resulting npm view pantheon-opencode dist-tags output.

Without that record, a later reader cannot tell a rollback apart from a failed publication.

docs.title: Retiring the next dist-tag
docs.text:
Manual step with human approval. Not part of the automated release workflow.

next was the pre-stable preview channel. Once stable v1.6.0 is published and verified it has no remaining purpose, and leaving it in place invites new releases to be tagged into a channel nobody resolves. It is removed exactly once.

Prerequisite: the post-publication verification of the stable release passed — npm view pantheon-opencode dist-tags reports latest = 1.6.0, and installing pantheon-opencode@1.6.0 from the public registry works. Removing next before that check leaves consumers who follow next without a resolution target while the stable channel is still unproven.

# Only after the post-publication verification passed.
npm dist-tag rm pantheon-opencode next

# Prove the result: latest = 1.6.0, beta preserved, next absent.
npm view pantheon-opencode dist-tags

Syntax: npm dist-tag rm <package-spec> <tag> (npm dist-tag --help).

The removal only drops a tag — no published version is deleted. beta continues to point at the beta line and is not touched by this step.

docs.title: Branch protection (main)
docs.text: The main protection policy — required checks, admin bypass, and the manual enable/verify procedure — lives in Branch Protection. The release job still re-runs the six gates on the frozen TARGET_SHA; protection does not replace them.

docs.title: Pre-Release Checklist
docs.text:
Before cutting a release, verify:

  • [ ] node scripts/versioning.mjs status shows a pending release (tag < pkg)
  • [ ] CHANGELOG.md has a ## [X.Y.Z] - date entry for the new version
  • [ ] Version manifests match: package.json == plugin.json == pyproject.toml == src/plugins/tui/package.json
  • [ ] All required checks green on the bump PR and on the push run for the merged main SHA (validate, test-suite, plugin-v2-ts-coverage, commitlint, security-scan, CodeQL)
  • [ ] The six release gates are expected to PASS for the frozen TARGET_SHA; the dispatch's validate job is the authority (it re-runs all six)
  • [ ] npm run release:dry-run passes (status + pack)

docs.title: Consumption Options
docs.text: Method Best for How npm package Dev workflow / CI npm install pantheon-opencode (stable) or npm install pantheon-opencode@beta Pantheon Installer New / existing projects npx pantheon-opencode init GitHub Release Downloads / CI Source archives from Releases page GitHub Template New projects "Use this template" on GitHub Git clone + copy Selective setup git clone and copy only what you need

docs.title: Release Assets
docs.text:
Each release includes:

Asset Description Source code (zip) GitHub auto-generated Source code (tar.gz) GitHub auto-generated pantheon-opencode@<ver> on npm Published with latest (stable) or beta dist-tag, provenance-signed

docs.title: Preserved Releases: Zenodo
docs.text:
Zenodo preserves releases for citation and long-term access through the official Zenodo ↔ GitHub integration on ils15/pantheon-opencode. Each published GitHub Release is archived automatically as a new version, giving that release a version DOI; all versions share the stable concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22650136 (conceptrecid 22650136), which always resolves to the latest archived release.

The integration has no pre-release filter: it archives every GitHub Release. Only the stable channel creates a GitHub Release, so only stable versions are archived. Beta releases create a git tag and publish to npm but no Release, and are therefore intentionally absent from the Zenodo family.

.zenodo.json is the source of the deposited metadata (title, creators/ORCID, description, license, keywords, and related identifiers). scripts/versioning.mjs bumps its version, publication_date, and url alongside the other manifests on every release, so the file must stay in sync for the next archive. The deposited title is read from .zenodo.json at the tagged commit and is not applied retroactively to versions already archived.

The integration is configured in Zenodo and runs on Zenodo's side — no workflow, token, or protected environment is stored in this repository. If a Release is not archived automatically, trigger a sync from the repository's Zenodo GitHub settings, then verify the concept DOI, the per-release version DOI, and the record metadata on Zenodo.

docs.title: Upgrading Pantheon
docs.text:
Português (Brasil)

This guide covers two moves: 1.5.2 → 1.6.0, which is an in-line upgrade, and 1.6.x → 2.x, which crosses the Pantheon support boundary. Supported host versions and evidence are in Compatibility; this page describes the actions.

docs.title: Upgrading from 1.5.2 to 1.6.0
docs.text:
Install globally first — update refuses local, workspace, and npx copies:

npm install -g pantheon-opencode@beta
pantheon-opencode update            # npm beta channel + config refresh
pantheon-opencode update --stable   # stable channel instead

update compares the installed version with the npm dist-tag, runs npm install -g pantheon-opencode@<channel>, then re-runs init --yes --headless so config merges, the Python venv, and MCP entries match the new package. Copy-only artifacts (agents, skills, AGENTS.md, commands, MCP scripts, code-mode payload) are refreshed by postinstall on every npm install.

After the update:

pantheon-opencode doctor

doctor warns when the package is newer than the last sync and detects plugin version drift when the registered path points into an older node_modules/pantheon-opencode copy.

If the update is interrupted, run init again. Every copy step is byte-compare idempotent, and the exact backup set under .pantheon/backups/<timestamp>/ is reversible with pantheon-opencode restore. Details are in Installation.

docs.title: What changes in 1.6.0
docs.text:
• The V2 tool surface is three unconditional tools — hashline_edit, pantheon_cost, pantheon_model — plus up to two host-dependent ones: vision_describe when the host exposes its model catalog, and pantheon_bounded_read when the host exposes its permission and session APIs (root Zeus sessions only). It is not six tools.
  • The three V2 goal tools are not registered. The goal loop needs a GoalStore, a GoalLoopClient, and a BackgroundJobBoard, none of which the V2 PluginContext exposes. The gap is reported as goal-tools.
  • Every V2 tool declares output. OpenCode 2.0.x rejects a tool whose declaration and result disagree.
  • V2 read-only sessions are enforced. A delegated apollo/gaia session is denied edit, write, bash, task, hashline_edit, and pantheon_model by the V2 execute.before hook.
  • Durable manual goals move to the Persistence MCP. goal_create, goal_get, goal_update, and goal_done are Zeus-only and session-scoped. V1 goal tools remain available but deprecated.
  • Step ceilings are stripped on V2 installs. steps is optional in OpenCode 2; an absent value means no native ceiling. Run the installer once to clear a stale value from a managed agent.
  • Memory gains a 64 KiB cap and TTL, and pantheon_cost reports USD by agent, model, and session from the models.dev catalog.

docs.title: Choosing the generation
docs.text:
npx pantheon-opencode init --opencode-version v1
npx pantheon-opencode init --opencode-version v2
npx pantheon-opencode init --opencode-version auto

auto is the default. --version v1|v2 remains accepted after init as the legacy spelling. The resolution order and fallback behavior are documented once in Compatibility. auto never installs both Pantheon plugin generations.

docs.title: Migration checklist
docs.text:
1. Stop OpenCode before changing the plugin generation.
  2. Run init once with the desired selector (v1, v2, or auto). Do not copy a V1 plugin entry into a V2 plugins list, or vice versa.
  3. If the TUI is wanted, include the installer plugins component. V1 uses tui.json; V2 uses its native local-plugin index.ts + tui.ts entrypoints. Installing the V2 server plugin alone does not install the TUI.
  4. Inspect the result: V1 Pantheon entries belong in plugin; the V2 Pantheon entry is the <installed>/src/plugin-v2 directory in plugins.
  5. Restart OpenCode after changing configuration.
  6. Run doctor and confirm no plugin-version drift remains.

docs.title: If the host lands on the wrong generation
docs.text: An install on the wrong generation means the gate could not read the host; it does not mean it guessed. Pass --opencode-version v2 explicitly, or set OPENCODE_VERSION=v2. To see what the gate reads, run opencode --version.

docs.title: Runtime differences after upgrading
docs.text:
• Delegation: neither generation registers a Pantheon-specific delegation tool. Use the host's native child-session engine — subagent in the reported root runtime, task() in host/API documentation. The former pantheon_delegate, pantheon_delegation_read, and pantheon_delegation_list tools were removed.
  • V1: ships hashline_edit, the goal/cost/model tools, the BackgroundJobBoard lifecycle, and the V1 event/tool/compaction hooks.
  • V2: does not register the BackgroundJobBoard, V1 event/tool hooks, or a Pantheon V1 compaction hook. It adds the V2 hooks documented in OpenCode V2.
  • Recovery: on restart, old or running V1 board jobs are marked errored; they are not auto-resumed and child work is not restarted automatically. V2 adds no automatic resume/restart behavior.
  • Reports: .pantheon/delegations/ Markdown reports are historical V1 board output, not a V2 task protocol.

Do not describe this upgrade as a V1-to-V2 feature-parity migration. It is a choice between a legacy runtime plugin and a narrower, host-native adapter.

docs.title: Outlook: 1.6.x to 2.x
docs.text:
From 1.7 onward Pantheon drops the V1 contract and targets OpenCode 2 only. OpenCode 1.X hosts are not supported on 2.x. OpenCode 2 support is already present in 1.6.x, so the 2.x change is a removal of the V1 path rather than a new host requirement.

Prepare for 2.x by:

  • moving durable manual goals to the Persistence MCP goal_* tools;
  • replacing any reliance on V1 goal tools or the BackgroundJobBoard;
  • confirming the installation is registered through plugins with the <installed>/src/plugin-v2 directory;
  • running doctor and the V2 sandbox checks described in Release Process.

docs.title: Historical upgrade notes
docs.text:
These notes are superseded and retained for users coming from older lines.

  • v1.0 removed all multi-platform support; Pantheon runs only on OpenCode. Installation moved to npx pantheon-opencode init.
  • v3.19.0 introduced the Memory Persistence Protocol. Its mandatory per-agent recall/store rules are historical: current policy searches only when project history could change the outcome, reuses coordinator results across delegation, and stores at most one reusable top-level outcome when a permitted write tool exists. See Memory.
  • OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_BACKGROUND_SUBAGENTS=true is not a universal prerequisite. It is an experimental gate for some runtimes and is set by Pantheon's npm run start launcher; use it only when the runtime documents and requires it.

For version-by-version detail, see the changelog.

docs.title: Atualização do Pantheon
docs.text:
English

Este guia cobre dois movimentos: 1.5.2 → 1.6.0, uma atualização dentro da linha, e 1.6.x → 2.x, que cruza a fronteira de suporte do Pantheon. As versões de host suportadas e a evidência estão em Compatibilidade; esta página descreve as ações.

docs.title: Atualizando de 1.5.2 para 1.6.0
docs.text:
Instale globalmente primeiro — update recusa cópias local, workspace e npx:

npm install -g pantheon-opencode@beta
pantheon-opencode update            # canal beta do npm + refresh de config
pantheon-opencode update --stable   # canal estável

update compara a versão instalada com a dist-tag do npm, executa npm install -g pantheon-opencode@<channel> e roda de novo init --yes --headless para que merges de config, o venv Python e as entradas MCP correspondam ao pacote novo. Artefatos de cópia (agents, skills, AGENTS.md, commands, scripts MCP, payload code-mode) são atualizados pelo postinstall em todo npm install.

Depois da atualização:

pantheon-opencode doctor

doctor avisa quando o pacote é mais novo que a última sincronização e detecta drift de versão do plugin quando o caminho registrado aponta para uma cópia antiga em node_modules/pantheon-opencode.

Se a atualização for interrompida, rode init de novo. Cada passo de cópia é idempotente por comparação de bytes, e o conjunto de backup exato em .pantheon/backups/<timestamp>/ é revertido com pantheon-opencode restore. Detalhes em Instalação.

docs.title: O que muda na 1.6.0
docs.text:
• A superfície de tools V2 é de três tools incondicionais — hashline_edit, pantheon_cost, pantheon_model — mais até duas dependentes do host: vision_describe quando o host expõe o catálogo de modelos, e pantheon_bounded_read quando o host expõe as APIs de permissão e sessão (apenas sessões raiz do Zeus). Não são seis tools.
  • As três tools de goal do V2 não são registradas. O loop de goal precisa de GoalStore, GoalLoopClient e BackgroundJobBoard, que o PluginContext V2 não expõe. A lacuna é reportada como goal-tools.
  • Toda tool V2 declara output. O OpenCode 2.0.x rejeita uma tool cuja declaração e resultado não concordam.
  • Sessões read-only do V2 são aplicadas. Uma sessão delegada de apollo/gaia recebe deny para edit, write, bash, task, hashline_edit e pantheon_model pelo hook execute.before do V2.
  • Goals manuais duráveis passam para o MCP de Persistence. goal_create, goal_get, goal_update e goal_done são exclusivos do Zeus e escopados por sessão. As tools de goal V1 continuam disponíveis, mas depreciadas.
  • Tetos de passos são removidos em instalações V2. steps é opcional no OpenCode 2; ausente significa nenhum teto nativo. Rode o instalador uma vez para limpar um valor antigo de um agente gerenciado.
  • A memória ganha cap de 64 KiB e TTL, e pantheon_cost reporta USD por agente, modelo e sessão a partir do catálogo models.dev.

docs.title: Escolhendo a geração
docs.text:
npx pantheon-opencode init --opencode-version v1
npx pantheon-opencode init --opencode-version v2
npx pantheon-opencode init --opencode-version auto

auto é o padrão. --version v1|v2 continua aceito depois de init como a grafia legada. A ordem de resolução e o comportamento de fallback estão documentados uma única vez em Compatibilidade. auto nunca instala as duas gerações do plugin Pantheon.

docs.title: Checklist de migração
docs.text:
1. Pare o OpenCode antes de trocar a geração do plugin.
  2. Rode init uma vez com o seletor desejado (v1, v2 ou auto). Não copie uma entrada de plugin V1 para uma lista plugins V2, nem o contrário.
  3. Se quiser a TUI, inclua o componente plugins do instalador. V1 usa tui.json; V2 usa os entrypoints nativos index.ts + tui.ts. Instalar apenas o plugin de servidor V2 não instala a TUI.
  4. Inspecione o resultado: entradas Pantheon V1 ficam em plugin; a entrada V2 é o diretório <installed>/src/plugin-v2 em plugins.
  5. Reinicie o OpenCode depois de mudar a configuração.
  6. Rode doctor e confirme que não resta drift de versão do plugin.

docs.title: Se o host cair na geração errada
docs.text: Uma instalação na geração errada significa que o gate não conseguiu ler o host; não significa que ele adivinhou. Passe --opencode-version v2 explicitamente, ou defina OPENCODE_VERSION=v2. Para ver o que o gate lê, rode opencode --version.

docs.title: Diferenças de runtime após a atualização
docs.text:
• Delegação: nenhuma geração registra uma tool de delegação específica do Pantheon. Use o motor nativo de sessões filhas do host — subagent no runtime raiz relatado, task() na documentação de host/API. As antigas pantheon_delegate, pantheon_delegation_read e pantheon_delegation_list foram removidas.
  • V1: traz hashline_edit, as tools de goal/cost/model, o ciclo de vida do BackgroundJobBoard e os hooks V1 de evento/tool/compaction.
  • V2: não registra o BackgroundJobBoard, hooks V1 de evento/tool nem um hook de compaction V1. Ele adiciona os hooks V2 documentados em OpenCode V2.
  • Recuperação: ao reiniciar, jobs antigos ou em execução do board V1 são marcados como erro; não são retomados automaticamente e o trabalho filho não reinicia sozinho. O V2 não adiciona retomada/reinício automático.
  • Relatórios: os relatórios Markdown em .pantheon/delegations/ são saída histórica do board V1, não um protocolo de tarefa V2.

Não descreva esta atualização como uma migração de paridade V1→V2. É uma escolha entre um plugin de runtime legado e um adaptador mais estreito, nativo do host.

docs.title: Perspectiva: 1.6.x para 2.x
docs.text:
A partir da 1.7, o Pantheon abandona o contrato V1 e mira apenas o OpenCode 2. Hosts OpenCode 1.X não são suportados na 2.x. O suporte a OpenCode 2 já existe na 1.6.x, então a mudança da 2.x é a remoção do caminho V1, não um novo requisito de host.

Prepare-se para a 2.x:

  • movendo goals manuais duráveis para as tools goal_* do MCP de Persistence;
  • removendo qualquer dependência das tools de goal V1 ou do BackgroundJobBoard;
  • confirmando que a instalação está registrada em plugins com o diretório <installed>/src/plugin-v2;
  • rodando doctor e as checagens de sandbox V2 descritas no Processo de release.

docs.title: Notas históricas de atualização
docs.text:
Estas notas estão superadas e são mantidas para quem vem de linhas antigas.

  • v1.0 removeu todo o suporte multiplataforma; o Pantheon roda apenas no OpenCode. A instalação passou a ser npx pantheon-opencode init.
  • v3.19.0 introduziu o Memory Persistence Protocol. As regras obrigatórias de recall/store por agente são históricas: a política atual busca apenas quando o histórico do projeto pode mudar o resultado, reutiliza resultados do coordenador nas delegações e grava no máximo um resultado reutilizável de nível superior quando existe uma tool de escrita permitida. Veja Memória.
  • OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_BACKGROUND_SUBAGENTS=true não é pré-requisito universal. É um gate experimental de alguns runtimes e é definido pelo launcher npm run start do Pantheon; use apenas quando o runtime documentar e exigir.

Para detalhe versão a versão, veja o changelog.

docs.title: MCP Tool Registry
docs.text:
Canonical reference for Pantheon agents. Lists every tool across the 5 native MCP servers, with signatures, descriptions, and which agents use them.

Agent tip: OpenCode exposes an MCP tool as {server}_{tool}. See Naming in OpenCode below.

docs.title: Servers
docs.text: Pantheon provides 5 native MCP servers. See below for full tool registries.

docs.title: pantheon-resources (read-only)
docs.text:
Read-only resource server. No tools — read resources directly via pantheon:// URIs using read_mcp_resource.

Resource URI Description pantheon://agents List all 14 agent definitions (YAML frontmatter) pantheon://agents/{name} Single agent config by name (case-insensitive) pantheon://routing Full routing.yml — delegation rules, handoff contracts pantheon://skills List all skills with descriptions pantheon://skills/{name} Specific skill SKILL.md content pantheon://deepwork/{slug} Deepwork PLAN.md pantheon://deepwork/{slug}/status Deepwork STATUS.md (defaults to IN_PROGRESS) pantheon://memory-bank/{path} Any file under .pantheon/memory-bank/ (path traversal blocked) pantheon://eval Latest plugin/skill certification scores from the plugin_eval namespace pantheon://eval/{plugin} Latest certification report for one plugin/skill

Used by: ALL agents. Common reads: routing (zeus, athena), agents/{name} (any), skills/{name} (implementers), memory-bank/{path} (aphrodite, mnemosyne), and eval reports when needed.

pantheon://memory-bank/{path} reads project files on demand; it does not auto-load them. The eval resources are registered by this server and read the global Memory SQLite database (PANTHEON_HOME / XDG_CONFIG_HOME override the default ~/.config/opencode/memory/memory.db) in the plugin_eval namespace. This namespace is not an access-control boundary: clients that can read the resources server can read the reports, and unfiltered memory_search calls can match entries from plugin_eval too.

Call pattern: 

read_mcp_resource(server="pantheon-resources", uri="pantheon://routing")

docs.title: pantheon-memory (persistent storage)
docs.text:
Lexical memory with SQLite FTS5 (BM25). The canonical source, src/mcp/memory_mcp.py, registers 9 tools: 6 memory_* tools for storing, searching, recalling, forgetting, listing, and inspecting entries, plus 3 code_* codemap operations. scripts/memory_mcp.py is a compatibility entrypoint that delegates to this canonical implementation. The runtime installer copies the canonical source into the installed scripts directory; install-mcp.mjs prefers that installed script and falls back to the source-tree entrypoint when running from a checkout. Keyword retrieval only — no embedding or vector index. The Memory server registers no resources.

Tool Signature Description Who uses it memory_store (value, namespace?: "default", key?, metadata?: "{}", ttl_seconds?) Store a reusable memory entry (FTS5 index updated by trigger); metadata is a JSON string. Over-cap writes are rejected, never truncated (see entry cap and expiry). ttl_seconds gives the entry a lifetime; on success returns {id, namespace, key, status, expires_at}, where expires_at is null when the entry does not expire Mnemosyne when durable context is warranted and write access is granted memory_search (query, namespace?, top_k?: 5, decay_days?, include_expired?: false) FTS5 BM25 keyword search (stopwords dropped, 4+ char terms prefix-matched); top_k is clamped to 1–50. Expired entries are filtered in SQL before LIMIT, so they cannot consume a candidate slot; include_expired=true opts back in. Optional freshness decay via decay_days (default off) only re-ranks, it does not expire. Empty results mean nothing matched; structured errors mean the memory store could not be read. Coordinator or specialist only when prior project context is relevant memory_recall (key, namespace?: "default") Exact recall of an entry by key within a namespace, including expires_at. Expiry is ignored on purpose: an expired entry is still returned (see entry cap and expiry) Exact-key lookup when needed memory_forget (id?, key?, namespace?: "default", expired_only?: false) Delete an entry by ID or key (FTS index cleaned via trigger), or purge every expired entry with expired_only=true — the only path that removes expired rows. Returns {deleted, purged, expired_only} on the purge path; not combinable with id/key Mnemosyne only — expiry purge is explicit maintenance memory_list (namespace?, prefix?, limit?: 50) List entries chronologically with namespace and key-prefix filters; limit is clamped to 1–500. Still lists expired entries, because this maintenance view is how they are inspected before purging Mnemosyne — explicit maintenance memory_stats () Database statistics: total_entries, namespaces, db_size_bytes, db_size_human, plus payload-size accounting — max_entry_bytes (cap in force), warning_threshold_bytes (half the cap, minimum 1 byte), total_bytes (summed serialized entry bytes), oversized_entries (count above the warning threshold) and largest_entries (up to 5 {namespace, key, bytes}) Mnemosyne — explicit maintenance code_index (path?, force?) Index codebase files into a knowledge graph (hash-based skip) No agent — blocked by design code_query (query, type?, limit?: 10) Search code entities via FTS5 apollo, athena code_neighbors (entity_id, depth?: 1) Graph neighbors of a code entity (BFS depth 1-3) apollo, athena

docs.title: memory_search result and error contract
docs.text:
A successful search returns an array; no matches (including an empty or all-stopword query) return []. A failure to open or read the memory store returns this JSON object as normal tool result content:

{"error":{"type":"MemorySearchError","message":"Memory search failed while reading the SQLite FTS index or stored entries. Check the memory store and FTS index, then retry."}}

The type is DatabaseUnavailableError when the database cannot be opened or MemorySearchError when search reads fail. The message is sanitized and does not contain filesystem paths, SQL, or raw exception text. MCP isError remains false because this is a returned data envelope, not a protocol-level tool exception. Callers should parse the returned JSON content and distinguish an array (including [], a successful search) from an object with an error key (a failed search); do not use isError or an empty array alone to detect this failure.

docs.title: Entry cap, expiry and purge contract
docs.text:
Size. A write is rejected when the serialized entry — value, metadata, namespace and key as UTF-8 — exceeds the per-entry cap: 65,536 bytes (64 KiB) by default, the same bound the Persistence MCP applies to checkpoint content. Set PANTHEON_MEMORY_MAX_ENTRY_BYTES in the memory server's environment to change the cap; it is read on every write, accepts any positive integer, and an unparseable or non-positive value falls back to 64 KiB. An over-cap write is rejected, never truncated — a shortened memory is silent data loss — and the error states the actual size, the cap in force, and that variable with an actionable value. The per-entry size behind memory_stats (total_bytes and largest_entries[].bytes) is measured the same way, so oversized_entries and the write guard agree.

Expiry. memory_store(ttl_seconds=...) accepts 1 to 31,536,000 seconds (365 days) and stores an ISO-8601 UTC expires_at. Omitting it stores NULL, meaning "never expires" — which is how every entry written before TTL support behaves. An entry is expired when expires_at is non-null and at or before the current UTC time.

What expiry changes. memory_search excludes expired entries by default and filters them in SQL before LIMIT, so an expired row cannot consume one of the candidate slots; include_expired=true returns them. memory_recall and memory_list still expose expired entries: null is already the answer for a key that does not exist, so hiding an expired entry from exact recall would make "expired" indistinguishable from "never existed", and the maintenance listing is how an operator inspects them before purging. decay_days is unrelated to expiry — it only multiplies BM25 scores by a freshness factor.

Explicit purge. No read deletes a row. memory_forget(expired_only=true) deletes every entry whose expires_at has passed, across all namespaces, returns {deleted, purged, expired_only}, is idempotent (purged: 0 once drained), cannot be combined with id/key, and never touches entries with a NULL expiry.

Older databases. A memory.db created before TTL support is upgraded on open: the server checks PRAGMA table_info(memories) and runs ALTER TABLE memories ADD COLUMN expires_at TEXT only when the column is missing, then creates its index with IF NOT EXISTS. A second open is a no-op, no row is rewritten or dropped, and no migration command is required from the user.

Apollo and Athena receive only the read-only code map operations (code_query, code_neighbors). No agent is granted code_index; its server-side path-confinement guard remains defense in depth.

These are exact per-agent mcp_tools.pantheon-memory frontmatter grants:

Agent(s) Exact pantheon-memory grant Apollo, Athena [memory_search, code_query, code_neighbors] Mnemosyne [memory_recall, memory_store, memory_search, memory_forget, memory_list, memory_stats] Aphrodite, Demeter, Hephaestus, Hermes, Nyx, Prometheus, Themis, Zeus [memory_search] Gaia, Iris, Talos [memory_recall]

Only Apollo and Athena receive code_query and code_neighbors; no agent receives any other code_* tool, including code_index. Zeus and all other agents receive no code_* tools. These are tools on pantheon-memory, not Code Mode, and do not include execute_code_script.

Lean call pattern: 

# Only when prior history can change the work; pass useful hits to child agents.
memory_search(query="existing auth patterns", top_k=2)

# Store once at the top level only if the result is reusable in a later session.
memory_store(value="Refresh tokens rotate on every use", key="decision-42")

The plugin_eval namespace shares this Memory database. Eval scripts write certification entries there; the pantheon-resources server exposes them via pantheon://eval and pantheon://eval/{plugin}. Namespaces organize queries but do not enforce access: unfiltered Memory searches can include eval entries, and access to the resource URIs follows access to the resources server.

The table describes server capabilities, not per-agent grants. Agent allowlists and runtime tool exposure can differ; inspect the active tool grants/catalog before relying on a tool. Temporary context_save/context_get checkpoints are not durable-memory writes. Use only tools exposed and permitted in the active context, and never claim a memory decision was persisted unless memory_store succeeds.

memory_store writes submitted values and metadata; automatic secret scrubbing/redaction is not guaranteed. Do not store secrets, credentials, or tokens.

Do not search at every agent start, repeat a task-level search in each child, or store routine phase/test summaries. Use memory_recall only when an exact key is already known; do not search and then immediately recall the same entry.

docs.title: pantheon-persistence (session checkpoints + manual goals)
docs.text:
The MCP server exposes exactly 6 tools. SQLite's KV table remains an internal implementation detail used by checkpoint storage; the former KV management, search, context-list/statistics, rehydration, and session-summary tools are not registered.

Use pantheon-memory for durable knowledge. Persistence stores explicit session-scoped checkpoints and manual goals; it is not the default cache for agent handoffs. Expired checkpoints are filtered on reads, not automatically purged.

Tool Signature Description Who uses it context_save (slug, key, content, session_id, ttl?, scope?, revision?) Save a bounded session checkpoint and update its latest pointer Zeus context_get (slug, key?, session_id?, legacy?, scope?) Read session-qualified checkpoint content Zeus goal_create (title, description?) Create the caller session's active manual goal Zeus goal_get (goal_id?) Read the caller session's active or latest completed goal Zeus goal_update (goal_id, expected_version, title?, description?, clear_description?) Edit goal fields with optimistic version checking Zeus goal_done (goal_id, expected_version) Complete the caller session's goal Zeus

Goal tools are Zeus-only because goals are session-scoped and cannot be read across sessions. Athena and Themis run in child sessions and cannot read Zeus's goal; as root they cannot create a goal in their own session because only Zeus has goal_create. Manual goals do not enable automatic continuation and do not replace the V1 GoalStore. See Memory for details.

docs.title: pantheon-code-mode (script execution)
docs.text:
Confined automation scripts from .pantheon/code-mode/. One tool, 30s timeout, .sh and .py only.

The server also registers pantheon://code-mode/scripts and pantheon://code-mode/scripts/{name} resources; these are not part of pantheon-resources.

Tool Signature Description Who uses it execute_code_script (script_name: str, args?: list[str]) Run a script from .pantheon/code-mode/ and return output Agents with bash: allow (zeus, hermes, aphrodite, demeter, themis, prometheus, hephaestus, talos)

NOT available to: athena, apollo, gaia, iris, nyx, mnemosyne (no bash access).

Use cases by agent: | Agent | Typical scripts | |-------|----------------| | zeus | Orchestration sequences | | hermes | pytest, ruff check, ruff format | | aphrodite | npm test, biome check | | demeter | alembic upgrade head && pytest | | themis | Lint/quality check scripts during review | | prometheus | Docker builds, CI/CD pipeline scripts | | talos | Automated hotfix sequences, batch fixes |

Call pattern: 

execute_code_script("lint-and-test.sh", args=["backend/"])

docs.title: pantheon-vision (image analysis)
docs.text:
The local vision server accepts local paths, file: URIs, data URIs, and HTTP(S) image URLs. The plugin first tries its configured native gateway, then falls back to this MCP. Bifrost is not a default dependency; use it only through an explicit PANTHEON_VISION_TOOL or imageAnalysisTool setting.

Tool Signature Description vision_describe (path: str, prompt?: str, session_id?: str) Describe image content, visible text, layout, and objects vision_ocr (path: str, session_id?: str) Extract visible text while preserving line formatting vision_analyze (path: str, session_id?: str) Return image metadata, description, and OCR as JSON

Permission: ask is recommended because images or remote URLs are sent to the configured gateway. The server reads PANTHEON_OPENCODE_API_KEY or OPENCODE_API_KEY, then the OpenCode auth store; no API key is stored in the repository configuration.

docs.title: OpenCode plugin tools
docs.text:
These tools are provided by the OpenCode plugin, not by one of the five native MCP servers listed above.

Tool Arguments What it reports pantheon_model action?: status\|show\|set\|reset, plus action-specific agent/model/effort and optional scope: project V2 manual overrides are project-only: status reads project configuration, and the agent transform applies only explicit project per-agent model/variant overrides; global files are neither read nor applied. set/reset reject scope: global and any confirm/authorize_global fields before writing. Global overrides require separate explicit human authorization in a future surface and are not supported by this tool; flags in the same tool call are not approval. V2 ignores static preset markers and PANTHEON_MODEL_PRESET, leaving host defaults intact otherwise. Invalid or malformed project overrides preserve the host model and expose warnings via status. The V2 server plugin has no documented toast or other proactive user-visible notification API during transform, so no toast/proactive warning is promised. V1 behavior remains legacy. pantheon_cost days?: 1..365 (default 7), session?: <root session id>, refreshPricing?: boolean Read-only token totals and USD cost by agent and phase, by model, and by session, in a rolling days × 24-hour window from query time. It is not a calendar-day or session window.

Prices come from the public models.dev catalog (USD per 1M tokens: input, output, cache read and cache write), cached at <configDir>/cache/models-dev.json, where <configDir> follows the usual resolution — PANTHEON_HOME, else $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/opencode, else ~/.config/opencode. A tool call reads that cache and never waits on the network: a missing or older-than-24 h cache is refreshed in the background with a 3 s timeout and the report says the prices it used are stale. Only refreshPricing: true waits for that bounded refresh, and it is how new prices are forced. PANTHEON_COST_OFFLINE=1 forbids every network request on every path: the lazy background refresh is not scheduled, and refreshPricing: true is refused outright — the report then says Pricing: REFUSED, names this variable, and makes no request at all. An unknown or ambiguous model, or cache tokens with no published cache rate, read — and are excluded from the total, which then says (partial) — a model the catalog prices at zero stays $0.00, because an unknown model is never reported as free. Passing session scopes the whole report to that root session plus its descendant sessions, resolved through the parent_id links already in the database. Costs are catalog list prices, not a provider invoice; on V2 the phase can be unknown; and the node:sqlite CLI-fallback path still reports tokens only, with the report saying so.

docs.title: Cost backend and attribution
docs.text:
pantheon_cost prefers a read-only node:sqlite connection to the selected opencode.db (src/pantheon/cost-command.ts). When node:sqlite is unavailable in the host runtime — for example under Bun — the tool falls back to spawning node scripts/cost.mjs as a read-only subprocess. The fallback resolves a real Node binary, PANTHEON_NODE first and then node on PATH, verifies that it supports node:sqlite (Node >= 22.5), and runs the script with an argument array, never through a shell. If neither source resolves, the tool returns status: UNSUPPORTED. Database failures return a contract status such as UNAVAILABLE or CORRUPT_DATA and include diagnostic detail, including captured stderr when available.

Variable Default Purpose PANTHEON_NODE node from PATH Node >= 22.5 binary used only for the node:sqlite capability in the CLI fallback. An explicit path must exist and be executable, otherwise the tool fails fast PANTHEON_COST_OFFLINE unset Set to 1 to forbid every network request, including refreshPricing: true. The report uses the cached catalog only, an explicit refresh is refused with a Pricing: REFUSED notice naming this variable, and no socket is opened PANTHEON_COST_DB unset Absolute path to the database, checked before OPENCODE_DB OPENCODE_DB unset Absolute path to the database, checked before the XDG default

The database is resolved by path in this order: an explicit dbPath from the tool caller, PANTHEON_COST_DB, OPENCODE_DB, then the XDG default opencode.db. There is no per-version filename in that chain: opencode-v2.db is not a host 2.x database — it is a name a sandbox gives its own state database through OPENCODE_DB.

The v1/v2 distinction is the detected schema, not the file name. The report looks for the message and session_message tables and reads whichever the open database actually holds, because a migrated database carries both families at once. PANTHEON_OPENCODE_VERSION=v1|v2 selects no file: it only narrows an already-detected set to one table family, and fails fast when the value is invalid or the requested family is not there. A database carrying neither table returns CORRUPT_DATA; a ledger that exists but yields no readable tokens returns UNSUPPORTED, never a successful empty report.

The report always includes ## Cost by agent and adds ## Cost by model and ## Cost by session tables. A session row covers that session alone; passing session:<id> sums the root session and its descendants. An unpriced row reads — and is excluded from the total, which then says (partial).

docs.title: Naming in OpenCode
docs.text:
Pantheon runs only on OpenCode, which exposes an MCP tool as {server}_{tool} — for example pantheon-memory_memory_recall. The older multi-platform naming examples were removed with multi-platform support in v1.0.

In the Code Mode execute sandbox the visible catalog is a subset, not the registry above. Resolve a hidden tool by calling search() for its exact path and then invoking that path literally — passing the whole path string as a single key fails even though search() returned it.

docs.title: Permission Tiers
docs.text:
OpenCode MCP tool grants authorize an agent to call the server tools exposed to it. They are not an OS-level sandbox and do not constrain the MCP process's permissions under the host user's OS account. The API/data boundary is therefore not limited to the repository: granted pantheon-memory tools operate on the user's global Memory database (~/.config/opencode/memory/memory.db by default; PANTHEON_HOME / XDG_CONFIG_HOME can override the root). code_query and code_neighbors read that global database's code index. Its code_files table has no project column, so results can include entities from any project previously indexed on this machine; these grants do not provide per-project isolation. No agent is granted code_index; its server-side path-confinement guard is defense in depth, not a project-isolation boundary for query results. Granted pantheon-persistence checkpoint tools can operate on the user's global database (~/.config/opencode/persistence/global.db by default) or the active project database (.pantheon/persistence/project.db), according to the scopes exposed by those tools. Manual goal tools use the Persistence deployment database and partition by session ID; a global install shares it across projects. Grants gate calls to registered MCP operations; they do not restrict the process's underlying OS permissions.

Server Recommended Tier Rationale pantheon-resources allow Read-only, same trust boundary as repo pantheon-code-mode ask Executes scripts — needs user confirmation pantheon-memory Per-agent exact mcp_tools lists above Host grants authorize only each listed tool; they are not an OS sandbox, and Memory data/index records use the user-global database pantheon-persistence per-agent exact tools Checkpoint tools can use the user-global or project database; manual goals are session-scoped in the deployment database, shared across projects in a global install pantheon-vision ask Sends image input to the configured vision gateway

docs.title: Security Notes
docs.text:
• pantheon-resources — path traversal protection on memory-bank/{path}
  • pantheon-code-mode — only .sh/.py in .pantheon/code-mode/, 30s timeout, no ../ escape
  • pantheon-memory — SQLite data in ~/.config/opencode/memory/memory.db by default (PANTHEON_HOME / XDG_CONFIG_HOME can override it); agent tool grants determine which tools are available
  • pantheon-persistence — checkpoint database at ~/.config/opencode/persistence/global.db by default; project scope uses .pantheon/persistence/project.db. PANTHEON_HOME / XDG_CONFIG_HOME override the global root.
  • pantheon-vision — 25 MB image cap, supported-format validation, safe errors, and API-key redaction

See skill: mcp-security for complete rules.

docs.title: OpenCode V2
docs.text: OpenCode 2 gets the Pantheon V2 plugin: host-native tools, V2 hooks, and a native TUI surface. This page covers what a user sees. The plugin contract, tool-by-tool registration, and the delegation matrix are in Architecture; supported hosts and evidence are in Compatibility.

docs.title: Generation detection
docs.text: The installer selects one generation per installation. auto is the default and reads the host; --opencode-version v1|v2|auto overrides it. The resolution order and the exact fallback behavior live in Compatibility. V1 and V2 plugins are never registered together.

docs.title: Tools on V2
docs.text:
The V2 plugin registers tools through ctx.tool.transform(), not through the V1 plugin path. The exact list per generation, with source locators, is in Architecture. In user terms:

  • hashline_edit edits files by line-tag anchors instead of raw line numbers.
  • pantheon_cost reports tokens and USD by agent, model, and session.
  • pantheon_model shows, sets, or resets per-agent project-scoped model overrides.
  • vision_describe appears when the host exposes its model catalog.
  • pantheon_bounded_read appears when the host exposes its permission and session APIs, and only in a root Zeus session.

The three legacy goal tools are not registered on V2. Use the Persistence MCP goal_* tools for durable manual goals; see Memory.

docs.title: Per-agent MCP permissions
docs.text:
The installer reads each agent's mcp_tools allowlist and generates native per-agent permissions for both generations. On OpenCode 2.x the host evaluates a permissions rule whose action is <server>_* (or <server>_<tool>) with effect deny/allow. The V1-shaped permission.mcp.<server> key is not an action the host evaluates; the installer translates allow/deny into the former. ask is not expressible for MCP on that host — it hides the tool instead of prompting, so the installer emits no rule and warns.

Deny-by-default, the entrypoints, and custom-server setup are in MCP.

docs.title: Dispatch sidebar block
docs.text:
The native V2 sidebar shows the Pantheon version, active preset/source, git state, a Context block with thousands-separated tokens and <percent>% used of <window> (blue ≤25%, green ≤50%, yellow ≤90%, red above), $<spent> spent, and a muted cache <n>% · <n.n> tok/s line.

One aggregated Dispatch block covers the whole child set:

  • header ◈ Dispatch · <n> rodando · $<cost>, summing every child, live and finished;
  • one row per live child (⠸ <agent>·<kind> $<cost> <duration>, newest first, three then … +N rodando);
  • finished children rolled up per agent: ✓ <total> · $<sum> · <M> agentes (plus · <F> falhas when any child failed), up to three <agent> ×<count>·<kind> $<sum> rows and … +K $<sum> beyond — never one row per session.

The ·<kind> suffix says why the child exists: coun/plan/revw/hot/ disc from an explicit [council]/[plan]/[review]/[hotfix]/[discovery] prefix on the subagent description, otherwise from the agent (athena→plan, themis→revw, talos→hot, apollo→disc, anything else→oth). council is never inferred from an agent. A ~ after the kind marks a background child.

The block stays within eight lines and is omitted entirely when the session has no child. It is added with append claims: the native prompt footer keeps its own line, and Pantheon only appends ▸<preset> · ✦<n> ativos while delegations are running.

docs.title: /dispatch panel
docs.text:
/dispatch (also in the palette as Pantheon: Dispatch) opens pantheon.dispatch in the host's session.panel slot: a full-width view of the same delegation tree, rendered from the same collector as the sidebar block, so a child is never listed twice.

The header is ◈ Dispatch — <session> (+ [fullscreen]) with counters for the whole tree (2 rodando · 70 concluídos · 1 falha · $3.59; a zero counter is omitted) over one row per child — ⠋ prometheus plan $0.09 14m34s — running first, then most recent activity, with ✓/✗/○/? for completed/failed/interrupted/unknown. The detail pane shows the selected child's title or spawning description, short id, model, in/out/reasoning/cache tokens, kind evidence, and parent id; — means the host did not publish it.

Panels at least 72 columns put the detail beside the list; narrower ones stack it under the list and truncate per column. Keys are namespaced and bound (k/up, j/down, home, end, pageup, pagedown, enter, f, escape/q) and live inside the panel claim, so they stay inert while the panel is not focused. The list is paged at ten rows and selection is held by session id.

The panel reads only host-cached state — no session sync, no child message.list, no HTTP — and its 80 ms spinner tick exists only while the panel is open with something running. Opening it requires an open session; otherwise Pantheon toasts Abra uma sessão para ver o Dispatch instead of inventing a route. Jumping from a row to the child session is a documented TODO: no session router destination is verified for a child id.

docs.text:
When you ask for a plan or start /pantheon-deepwork, Athena returns the full plan to Zeus, who displays it in the main conversation before asking for approval. The approval prompt never points to a plan hidden in a child agent's conversation.
